current.text: Isaiah Stewart is gone from Detroit. Jalen Duren has signed and starts at center. Reed is the backup center in the bench rotation.
Duren's signing caps his upside. He should play about 20 minutes a night if Duren plays about 28.
He is Detroit's stash option behind Duren. If Duren misses time and Reed plays about 28 minutes, he could be a top 40 to top 50 player.
Last season he clearly outplayed Duren and Stewart in the regular season and the playoffs. The Pistons rate him above Stewart.

Experts still like him as a late pick. One ranks him around pick 120 to 13th round in 14-team leagues and calls his ESPN rank far too low. In a mock auction Josh said he likes him a lot, and he went for 4 USD.
Detroit plays 4-3-4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has 15 back-to-backs, but no rest risks are expected.

durable.text: He is an excellent per-minute producer.
He is not expected to carry a 30-minute starter's load.
He has always had high block rates per possession. 29% of his rim contests end in blocks.
He makes almost no threes. That is his weakest category, even for a big.

note: Our league drafts only 144 players, and he ranks 181 on Yahoo and 242 on ESPN. Neither site puts a price on him, so at most he is a 1 USD endgame handcuff for a Duren owner or a punt 3PM build. He gives about 58% FG on low volume, good blocks and steals for his minutes, and few turnovers. Early in the season, check whether he really gets about 20 minutes behind Duren and keep an eye on Duren's health. If he goes undrafted, he is a quick waiver add the moment Duren misses games.
